U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent announced Thursday that the Trump administration plans to sanction “a large bank” next week, ramping up economic pressure to force an end to the six-month conflict with Iran.

“We’re going to do it on Monday because we want to honor the memory of our fallen citizens on 9/11. But watch this space on Monday,” Bessent said during an appearance on “Real ​America’s Voice,” without naming the financial institution or the country.

The remarks come after Trump’s administration sanctioned the Dubai branches of the second-largest bank in Egypt, which is believed to have given Iranians $1.8B of funds. According to Bessent, Turkey’s largest bank “that had been giving to the Iranians” will also be closed.

The US has imposed a range of economic measures against Iran since the conflict began in February, targeting oil exports, shipping networks, weapons procurement channels, financial ​intermediaries, digital asset ​ exchanges, and ⁠aviation links.

title: Bessent: U.S. to sanction 'large bank' next week to pressure Iran
